title: 3PL vs. Dropshipping Considerations for Ecommerce Stores
summary: Explore the difference between 3PL vs. dropshipping to understand which fulfillment model makes the most sense for your business.
body_markdown:
When deciding how to get products to your customers, two options are third-party logistics (3PL) and dropshipping. Although both models involve outsourcing fulfillment without requiring your own warehouse, they differ in inventory ownership, upfront costs, supply chain control, and shipping speed.


Choosing the right fulfillment model can affect customer satisfaction, customer loyalty, and profitability. According to a[2026 AlixPartners survey](https://www.alixpartners.com/newsroom/press-release-alixpartners-2026-home-delivery-survey/) , more than 85% of US consumers say a poor delivery experience makes them less likely to shop with the same retailer again.


Learn the differences between 3PL fulfillment and dropshipping, compare what each costs, and evaluate which option best fits your business needs.


## What is 3PL?


[Third-party logistics](https://www.shopify.com/blog/3pl-ecommerce) , commonly abbreviated to 3PL, refers to using an outside partner to store inventory and ship orders to customers. When using a 3PL fulfillment service, you purchase or manufacture your own inventory upfront and arrange delivery to the provider’s warehouse space or network of[fulfillment](https://www.shopify.com/blog/ecommerce-fulfillment) centers.


The 3PL provider receives and stores your inventory, tracks stock levels, and handles[order fulfillment](https://www.shopify.com/blog/order-fulfillment) , including packing and[shipping](https://www.shopify.com/blog/order-fulfillment) orders. Depending on the provider and the warehouse management system you use, you can sync order information and tracking details automatically between the warehouse and your ecommerce platform.


Many 3PL providers offer additional services, including:


-


**Kitting and assembly.** Packing separate items or parts into a single box or custom set before sending them out.


-


**Custom packaging.** Using[branded packaging](https://www.shopify.com/blog/brand-packaging) , printed tissue paper, custom shipping boxes, and promotional inserts to create a branded unboxing experience.


-


**Returns management.** Processing returns, inspecting items for damage, restocking usable merchandise, and updating stock counts.


-


**B2B and wholesale freight fulfillment.** Preparing large wholesale shipments alongside direct-to-consumer orders for retailers expanding into physical stores.


[Shopify Fulfillment Network](https://www.shopify.com/fulfillment) connects you with vetted third-party logistics providers through the Shopify admin dashboard. You can compare fulfillment partners based on factors such as storage costs, order fulfillment fees, and shipping times.


## What is dropshipping?


[Dropshipping](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-dropshipping) is an order fulfillment method where an online store sells products without owning or holding inventory. When you receive customer orders through your ecommerce website, you purchase the merchandise directly from a third-party supplier—such as a manufacturer or wholesaler—that then packages and ships the product to the customer.


Because you don’t purchase inventory upfront, the[business model](https://www.shopify.com/blog/business-model) requires less[startup capital](https://www.shopify.com/blog/startup-capital) than buying products in bulk. You also avoid costs for warehouse space and holding inventory. Instead, you pay the supplier for individual items only after a customer places and pays for an order through your store.


If you run a[dropshipping business on Shopify](https://www.shopify.com/dropshipping) , you can manage operations through apps and marketplace integrations within the[Shopify App Store](https://apps.shopify.com/) .[DSers](https://apps.shopify.com/dsers) , for example, automates order syncing between your Shopify store and suppliers, while[print-on-demand](https://www.shopify.com/blog/print-on-demand) services such as[Printful](https://apps.shopify.com/printful) and[Gelato](https://apps.shopify.com/gelato-print-on-demand) let you sell customized apparel and home goods without holding inventory.


You can also use[Shopify Collective](https://www.shopify.com/collective) to sell products from other vetted Shopify brands, with suppliers fulfilling orders directly to customers.

## 3PL vs. dropshipping: Key differences


- Inventory ownership and capital investment
- Profit margins and cost structures
- Customer experience, packaging, and branding
- Shipping speed and transit times
- Quality control and returns management


The key differences between 3PL and dropshipping come down to how much you invest in inventory, what you pay for fulfillment, and how much control you have over the customer experience. Here’s a detailed breakdown:


### Inventory ownership and capital investment


A key distinction between 3PL and dropshipping is inventory ownership.


With a 3PL, you make or buy inventory in advance, which requires upfront capital, and pay the provider for[inventory storage](https://www.shopify.com/blog/inventory-storage) . Your inventory is a business[asset](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-an-asset) , but having too much ties up capital in unsold products, while too little can lead to stockouts and lost sales.


With dropshipping, you purchase products on demand as customers place orders. This reduces upfront inventory costs and the risk of unsold stock, allowing you to test new product lines and catalog expansions without committing to bulk purchases. However, you have less control over inventory availability and must rely on suppliers to keep products in stock.


### Profit margins and cost structures


For ecommerce businesses, 3PL and dropshipping have different cost structures, which can affect how much profit you earn on each sale.


With a 3PL, purchasing or manufacturing your merchandise in bulk can lower your cost per item and potentially increase[gross margins](https://www.shopify.com/blog/gross-margin) . However, those savings may be offset by ongoing third-party logistics fees, which include:


-


Receiving fees for unloading and processing incoming inventory


-


Monthly pallet or bin storage costs


-


[Pick-and-pack fulfillment](https://www.shopify.com/blog/pick-and-pack-fulfillment) fees per item or order


-


Packaging material costs and carrier shipping charges


Dropshipping involves fewer storage and fulfillment expenses, but you typically pay more for each item than you would when purchasing in bulk. Suppliers may also charge separately for packaging and shipping. Consequently, dropshipping can produce lower profit margins, leaving less room to absorb[customer acquisition costs](https://www.shopify.com/blog/customer-acquisition-cost) .


### Customer experience, packaging, and branding


A 3PL typically gives you more control over packaging and the post-purchase customer experience. Many third-party[fulfillment centers](https://www.shopify.com/blog/fulfillment-center) support custom packaging, branded shipping tape, personalized packing slips, and promotional inserts. These options help you create a consistent branded experience for customers.


Dropshipping generally offers fewer[branding](https://www.shopify.com/blog/product-branding) options because suppliers control how orders are packed and shipped. Some use generic packaging, making it harder to create a distinctive customer experience. Although some dropshipping suppliers offer custom packaging, they may charge additional fees or impose[minimum order quantities](https://www.shopify.com/blog/minimum-order-quantity) for branded materials.


### Shipping speed and transit times


Because many 3PLs operate warehouses across multiple locations, you can store products closer to major cities and shipping hubs. This distribution network can reduce transit times and enable faster ground shipping. For example,[ShipBob](https://www.shipbob.com/regional-distribution/) offers two-day shipping across the US through its fulfillment network.


Dropshipping fulfillment timelines depend on supplier locations, order processing times, and shipping methods. For example,[USA Drop](https://usadrop.com/aliexpress-standard-shipping/) estimates that standard shipping from AliExpress, a popular marketplace for dropshipping suppliers, takes 15 to 30 business days for delivery to the US.


Longer shipping times can increase the risk of customer complaints and chargebacks if orders arrive later than expected. Working with domestic dropshipping suppliers can result in faster shipping.


### Quality control and returns management


With a 3PL, you can arrange for products to be inspected before they’re shipped to customers. Some providers offer[quality control](https://www.shopify.com/blog/manufacturing-quality-control) services, such as checking incoming inventory for damage or defects. Returns can also be routed back to the 3PL facility, where staff can inspect and restock eligible items.


Dropshipping offers less control over product quality because suppliers manage the shipping process and send goods directly to customers. Although you can order samples to evaluate products before selling them, you can’t inspect individual orders before shipment.[Processing returns](https://www.shopify.com/blog/ecommerce-returns-management) can also be more complicated because you must coordinate with suppliers, whose return policies and procedures may vary.


## What to consider when choosing your fulfillment solution


Choosing between third-party logistics and dropshipping depends on your budget, sales volume, and business goals. Consider how much you can invest upfront, whether your sales are predictable, and how much control you want over fulfillment.


If you’re validating a new business idea or have limited capital, dropshipping lets you test[market demand](https://www.shopify.com/blog/market-demand) without investing in inventory upfront. This can be particularly useful when you’re unsure which products will sell.


If your store generates consistent, predictable sales, a 3PL may become more cost-effective for supporting business growth. Buying inventory in bulk can reduce per-unit costs, but you’ll need enough cash to cover those purchases and ongoing fulfillment fees. Compare your total costs under each model before making the switch.


If you sell proprietary products or custom-manufactured goods, a 3PL may be a better option because you can purchase inventory from your chosen manufacturer and have it stored and shipped by a fulfillment partner. Traditional dropshipping marketplaces primarily offer mass-manufactured goods available to multiple competing retailers, although services like print on demand also support original designs.


## 3PL vs. dropshipping FAQ


### Is Amazon a 3PL or 4PL?


Amazon offers 3PL services through[Fulfillment by Amazon (FBA)](https://www.shopify.com/blog/direct-fulfillment) and Amazon Multi-Channel Fulfillment (MCF), which storeinventory and fulfill orders for sellers. Fourth-party logistics (4PL) providers take on a broader role, coordinating multiple logistics partners and managing supply chain operations.


### What are the disadvantages of using a 3PL?


The disadvantages of using a 3PL include upfront inventory costs and ongoing fees for storage, intake, and order packing. Unsold products can also result in long-term storage fees eating into profits. Additionally, you depend on your fulfillment provider to pack and ship orders accurately and on time.


### What are the challenges of dropshipping?


Compared to traditional direct-to-consumer businesses, the challenges of dropshipping include potentially lower profit margins, limited control over product quality and branded packaging options, and longer shipping windows when using overseas suppliers. Because suppliers manage fulfillment, you also depend on them to maintain inventory, ship on time, and process returns according to their policies.
